algorithm_fidelity.derives_eom_from_vari.reason: lattice1d.py implements the Euler–Lagrange equations of the stated Yee-type action: a Wilson-line covariant Klein–Gordon update, charge and current densities as variational derivatives of S_d, and Maxwell–Ampère updates; lattice2d.py does the same in 2D. Methods 2.1 presents S_d and derives each equation of motion as δS_d=0, with the discrete Noether continuity law. The structural log confirms continuity to round-off.

algorithm_fidelity.yee_type_field_layout.reason: φ sits on vertices; A^x on x-edges (i+1/2); the optional temporal component sits on time-like edges at n+1/2 (temporal gauge is used); E_x lives on time-like faces. In 2D, A^x and A^y are on x- and y-edges and B_z is on plaquettes. In 1D the transverse A^y and A^z sit on vertices, which is the correct dimensional reduction of the y/z edges.

algorithm_fidelity.bianchi_identities_by.reason: B is computed only as the discrete curl of A, and A is advanced by A −= ΔtE, so the discrete Faraday law holds identically; ∇·B=0 is trivial in the 1D/2D reductions. Logged Faraday residuals are 3.8e-16 (1D) and ≤ 8.1e-15 in the periodic, Landau-twisted and symmetric-twisted 2D sectors, all ≪ 1e-10. Production-run logs do not record Faraday residuals separately, but the identity is structural to both solvers and verified in every boundary sector used.

boundary_boundary_test_2.fix_proposal_an.reason: The fix — band-limit the sampled fluctuations at |p| ≤ Λ and add a gauge-invariant counterterm δm² = −q²⟨A⊥²⟩_Λ — follows directly from the tadpole analysis: the band limit makes the tadpole finite and the counterterm cancels it.

boundary_boundary_test_2.fix_implementat.reason: The fix runs as a real code path: the dm2 counterterm in the KG update and energy (lattice1d.py), the band-limited samplers (vacuum.py), and an analytically computed counterterm (run_boundary_vacuum.py). boundary_boundary_test_2.fix_documented_.reason: The counterterm modifies the discrete Lagrangian (L_d → L_d − δm²φ̄φ), the modified KG equation includes δm², the preserved invariants (Noether charge, Bianchi, gauge invariance, variational structure) are stated, and the relaxed properties are given (bare ≠ physical mass, Λ as a physical scale, no physics above Λ). boundary_boundary_test_2.fix_resolves_fa.reason: Before and after: photon-vacuum m_eff/m goes from 1.079→1.106 (unfixed) to 1.0010, 0.9998, 0.9995, 0.9995 (fixed; spread 0.15%). E=0 spurious occupation goes from 0.052, 0.084, 0.161 to −0.0122, −0.0125, −0.0113, independent of Δx. At strong fields (qE = 2, 3) the repaired scheme stays near Nikishov (null-subtracted 0.87 and 0.98, versus 0.68 and 0.76 unrepaired); the fix is inactive (dm2 = 0) in non-vacuum runs using the same code. Caveats: with the matter vacuum also seeded, the fixed mass remains 1.10, 1.11, 1.08, 1.09 (logged but unreported), and the qE ~ m² yield is acknowledged as unusable.
